passage:
Sharmila to Aarav (brother)
Sharmila: Minakshi is such a nobody. She trips over her own bag lol
Sharmila: honestly she's fair game, everyone knows it
Aarav: why does she bother you so much
Sharmila: she doesn't. She's just weak
Aarav: then why do you keep talking about her
Sharmila: ...
Sharmila: because she cried in class and I felt sick
Aarav: sick like guilty?
Sharmila: sick like scared
Sharmila: if she can be that weak then maybe I could be too
Aarav: that's a lot to notice
Sharmila: I know. I was picked last for hockey last week and I laughed it off. I think I've been making her the weak one so it isn't me

qa.q: What did Sharmila say Minakshi trips over?
qa.a: Sharmila said Minakshi trips over her own bag.

qa.q: What does Sharmila realise is the real fear?
qa.a: Sharmila is scared of being weak too. Seeing Minakshi cry made Sharmila feel sick because it could have been Sharmila.

qa.q: What could Sharmila do next after this realisation?
qa.a: Sharmila could stop treating Minakshi as fair game, notice when the old story shows up, and keep talking with Aarav about the fear, and not turn contempt into a public habit.

qa.q: How might Minakshi feel when she is talked about this way?
qa.a: Minakshi might feel small and picked on; being called a nobody after crying in class would hurt.

grounding: Sharmila looks down on a weaker classmate and treats Minakshi as fair game, then recognises the contempt covers Sharmila's own fear of being weak.

passage:
On the school bus, Disha always sat at the back with her friends. Mohit, from Class 8, sat alone near the front. He was small, wore thick glasses, and hummed to himself.
"Fair game," Disha said, flicking paper balls at his head. "He's so weak. He won't even say anything." Her friends giggled.
One afternoon the bus conductor, Pramod bhaiya, stopped at the depot and asked Disha to stay behind. "Why him?" he asked.
"Because he's pathetic. He doesn't fight back."
"And what happens to someone who doesn't fight back?"
Disha felt a jolt. In her old school, she had been the small one. Girls had torn her notebooks and she hadn't fought back either. She had sworn never to be weak again.
She looked down. "I don't want to be like him," she said quietly. "Like I was."
"You're not weak if you're kind," Pramod bhaiya said. The next day, Disha sat at the back and threw nothing.

qa.q: What did Disha flick at Mohit's head?
What was Disha afraid of beneath her contempt for Mohit?
qa.a: She feared being weak again, as she had been when girls tore her notebooks at her old school.

qa.q: What helped Disha challenge her story about Mohit?
qa.a: Pramod bhaiya's questions made her see that her contempt covered her own fear, and she stopped throwing things.

qa.q: How might Mohit feel on the bus rides?
qa.a: Mohit likely feels anxious and humiliated, sitting alone while paper balls hit his head.

grounding: A teen who sees a weaker student as fair game challenges that story and sees it hides her fear of being weak herself.

passage:
Dhruv,
I don't know if you'll read this, but I'm writing it anyway.
All of Class 9, I called you "crybaby" in front of everyone. I made fun of your inhaler and your handwriting. I told myself you were fair game because you never fought back. I thought people like you were just weak.
Last week the counsellor asked me why I needed someone to look down on. I had no answer at first. Then I remembered being eight, when my cousins called me the weakling and locked me in the store room. I think I've been scared ever since of anyone seeing me as weak. So I made you the weak one instead.
That doesn't excuse it. I'm sorry. I've stopped, and I won't join in when others do it.
If you ever want to tell me how it felt, I'll listen.
Gautam

qa.q: What did Gautam call Dhruv in front of everyone?
What was Gautam afraid of, underneath the contempt?
qa.a: Gautam felt afraid of being seen as weak, a fear from being locked in the store room by cousins at eight.

qa.q: Which steps is Gautam taking now, and why are they wise?
qa.a: Gautam is apologising without excuses, has stopped the mocking and won't join in again, which ends the public habit of contempt.

qa.q: How might Dhruv feel reading the letter?
qa.a: Dhruv might feel wary and still hurt, but perhaps a little relieved that Gautam finally sees the harm.

grounding: A teen who looked down on a classmate as fair game recognises it hid a fear of being weak and apologises.
